Know your file

What is a scanned PDF?

Digital PDF

Made from Word, Google Docs or a website. You can select and copy the text. No OCR is needed: the standard converter keeps the layout.

Scanned PDF

Made with a scanner, a copier or a scanner app. Each page is a picture of paper, so trying to select the text does nothing. Converting it to Word needs OCR (optical character recognition).

Image or picture PDF

Phone photos, screenshots or pictures saved as a PDF. For a converter it is the same as a scan: the words are pixels, and OCR turns them back into text you can edit.

Not sure which one you have? Upload it: every page is checked, and OCR runs only on the pages that need it.

Under the hood

How our OCR turns a scan into editable Word text

1. Each page is checked

The converter looks at the visible text and the images on every page. A text page and a scanned page can sit in the same PDF; each one gets the right method.

2. The image is cleaned up

The sheet is cut out of the background, uneven light is flattened, contrast is raised, noise is removed and slightly tilted pages are straightened. The page is read at about 300 DPI.

3. The language is detected

A few lines are tested first to find the language (English, French, Arabic or a mix), then the whole page is read with it.

4. The structure is rebuilt

Lines are joined into real paragraphs, larger text becomes Word headings, and tables with clear ruled lines become Word tables.

5. No page is lost

A photo without text stays in the document as a picture. A page the OCR cannot read (handwriting, for example) is kept as an image with a short note, instead of wrong text.

6. One Word file

Everything is written into a standard .docx file in page order. Arabic paragraphs are set right to left, and Latin words inside them keep their direction.

Get a cleaner result

Tips for better OCR results

  • Scan at 300 DPI. Lower resolutions, and photos taken from far away, give more reading errors.
  • Keep pages straight and upright. Small tilts are corrected, but a page that is sideways or upside down is not.
  • Use even, flat light. Avoid shadows from your hand or phone, glare, and pages that curve near the binding.
  • Fill the frame with the page, one page per image, and keep the text sharp and in focus.
  • Printed text works; handwriting is not read reliably.
  • Long scan? Split it so each file stays under your scanned-page limit (50 pages with Pro, 20 free).

Languages

OCR in English, French and Arabic

English

Letters, forms, contracts, reports and course notes in English.

French

French documents with their accents (é, è, à, ç), and pages that mix French and English.

Arabic

Arabic scans become right-to-left Word paragraphs and tables. Pages that mix Arabic with French or English are supported.

Other languages are not supported yet: their text may come out wrong.

Before you upload

What the converter cannot do

  • JPG, PNG or HEIC photos: only PDF files are accepted. Make a PDF from your photos first (see below), then upload it.
  • Handwriting: it is not read reliably. Unreadable pages are kept as images with a note.
  • Password-protected PDFs: remove the password first. See password-protected PDF to Word.
  • An exact copy of the page: OCR gives you editable text, not the original picture. Complex layouts, columns and tables without grid lines may need a touch-up.
  • Files over the limits: more than 25 MB, or more scanned pages than your plan allows. Split the PDF into smaller parts.

How to make a PDF from photos first

  • iPhone or iPad: in the Files app, tap the three dots, then Scan Documents. Save the scan as a PDF.
  • Android: in the Google Drive app, tap +, then Scan. Drive saves the pages as a PDF.
  • Windows: select the photos, right-click and choose Print (on Windows 11, under Show more options), then pick the printer "Microsoft Print to PDF".
  • Mac: open the photos in Preview, then choose File, Export as PDF (or Print, then Save as PDF for several pages).

Then upload that PDF here: its photo pages are read with OCR like any scan.
